Executive Summary

Rerunning the validated rank-based screen on the recovered, deduplicated cohort materially changes the headline result.

Principal Finding — New

Public-contribution language is now a certifiable separator of admitted vs rejected applicants. public_contribution_count (a service + leadership composite) reaches Cliff’s δ = 0.395 (medium), 95% CI [0.16, 0.61], and survives every multiplicity correction — Benjamini-Hochberg (p = 0.015), Holm (0.015), and the dependence-aware Westfall-Young max-T (0.011). In the original study this same feature was the top lead but dissolved under correction (BH p = 0.142). This is exactly the outcome Report 4 (v1) predicted would follow from recovering rejected applicants.

The clearest way to see this finding is in plain odds: in a head-to-head matchup, the admitted applicant out-scores the rejected applicant on public-contribution language about 70 times out of 100 — versus a coin flip for a feature with no real effect.

Honest scope — one confirmed finding, not seven

Seven features clear the exploratory BH-FDR screen (q = 0.10), but this count is fragile and threshold-driven: only public_contribution_count survives the strict family-wise (Holm / Westfall-Young) bar. The other six — leadership, builder-signal, activity-hour entries, service, writing word count, prestige — are small effects (δ ≈ 0.24–0.29) that remain suggestive, not proven. The presence of writing_word_count (a text-length confounder) in that same tier is a warning that the small-δ semantic passers partly track essay length, not content.

Attribution — we stress-tested the jump

The improvement is driven by both the recovery and the deduplication, and — importantly — the original null was partly an artifact of pseudoreplication, not only low power:

Cohortnadmitreject public_contribution BH p# passing BH q=.10
v1 raw — original published10980290.1420
v1 deduplicated — dedup effect only10277250.0672
v2 raw — recovery effect only13497370.0461
v2 deduplicated — promoted cohort12794330.0157

Recovery alone and dedup alone each push public_contribution to significance; together they compound. The “7 passers” appears only in the combined cohort and should be read as BH step-up amplification once one very small p-value enters, not as seven independent discoveries.

Bottom line

The project now has its first feature that reliably distinguishes admitted from rejected Purdue applicants in this cohort — civic / public-contribution language — with everything else still in the exploratory tier.

1.Cohort Construction

What “promote v2” changed:

  • Source: purdue_semantic_features_v2.csv (134 rows = 109 baseline + 25 recovered; recovered rows verified, all distinct Common App IDs).
  • Deduplication (new in this rerun): collapsed to one row per applicant by CAID. The baseline matched table carried pre-existing duplicates that the original n = 109 study silently included:
    • 5 duplicate-PDF / multi-cycle pairs collapsed to one row each (Jay Yeung, Ryland Hsiang, Mingshi Liu, Janice Chin, Justin Zhang).
    • 1 applicant dropped — Vibhu Krishnan — whose two rows carried contradictory labels (Accepted and Rejected, same cycle, identical features). One feature vector assigned to both classes is uninterpretable for a rank test and maximally anti-signal; removing it is a correctness fix, not a convenience.
  • Result: n = 127, 94 admitted / 33 rejected (admit base rate 74%).
  • Reproduce the pre-promotion row-based cohort with load_cohort(dedup = FALSE).

Relative to the original Report 4 (80 / 29), the rejected class grew from a deduplicated baseline of 25 to 33 (+32%); the originally reported “29 rejects” was inflated by ~4 pseudoreplicated / contradictory rows.

2.Methods

Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum via admit-group rank sum; 10,000-permutation exact null; Cliff’s δ effect size with stratified percentile bootstrap 95% CI; multiplicity via Benjamini-Hochberg (q = 0.10, exploratory screen), Holm and Westfall-Young max-T (FWER α = 0.05, confirmatory). 19 features in three tiers (12 semantic, 4 intensity, 3 exposure / confounder). Identical to v1 — only the cohort changed.

How to read the evidence tiers

Every result in this report is graded into one of four tiers, used consistently across all charts:

Confirmed — survives strict family-wise correction Suggestive — passes the exploratory screen only Confounder — tracks essay / word length No evidence — confidence interval includes zero

Cliff’s δ is the effect size: the probability a random admit out-scores a random reject, rescaled to [−1, +1]. δ = 0.40 means the admitted applicant wins roughly 70 of 100 head-to-head matchups.

3.Statistical Power

Noether approximation for the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test, n₁ = 94, n₂ = 33 (vs original 80 / 29):

Cliff’s δMagnitude Power, single test (new)(original)Power, strict 19-test
0.15negligible~25%~22%~4%
0.25small~57%~51%~19%
0.33medium~80%~75%~42%
0.395(observed top)~92%~88%~64%
0.50large~99%~98%~90%

The cohort is now well-powered (≈80%) for medium effects and ~57% for small ones; the binding constraint remains the 33 rejects. public_contribution at δ = 0.395 has ~92% single-test power and ~64% even under a strict 19-way correction — consistent with its survival of Westfall-Young.

5.Findings by Evidence Tier

A. Confirmed — medium effect, CI excludes 0, survives FWER: one

public_contribution_count — δ = 0.395, CI [0.16, 0.61]; admitted applicants show stochastically more service / leadership language (P(admit > reject) ≈ 70%). Robust to Holm and Westfall-Young. This is the project’s first certifiable semantic separator.

The confirmed effect is a distributional shift, not a hard threshold — the groups overlap, but admitted applicants sit consistently higher:

Read as a strategy exhibit, admission rate climbs steadily with each public-contribution quartile — while still carrying the associational guardrail:

B. Suggestive — pass exploratory BH, fail FWER: five semantic / intensity features

Leadership, builder-signal, activity-hour entries, service, prestige. They form a coherent civic-contribution + activity-engagement cluster (which is why they move together and why dependence-aware correction is the right bar). Promising, not proven.

These features co-vary as one underlying theme — and essay length correlates with all of them, which is what keeps the cluster unconfirmed:

C. Confounder caution

writing_word_count passes BH at δ = 0.261 — comparable to the suggestive semantic features. Because longer text mechanically inflates term counts, the Tier-B small effects cannot be cleanly separated from text-length exposure on this evidence. public_contribution (δ = 0.395, WY-significant) stands clearly above the confounder; the Tier-B features do not.

D. No evidence — CI includes 0

The remaining features, including CS/AI, STEM-signal, and research — consistent with v1.

6.Corrections to Prior Claims

Carried forward + new:

  1. CS/AI remains a non-separator (δ = 0.18, CI includes 0). The v1 correction stands.
  2. Research remains the least discriminating feature (δ = 0.04). The v2-model’s strong negative coefficient was an artifact, as Report 4 (v1) concluded.
  3. New — the v1 “no significant feature” conclusion is now superseded: with recovered rejects and removal of pseudoreplication, public-contribution language clears all corrections. Part of the v1 null was a pseudoreplication artifact (dedup alone moved BH 0.142 → 0.067), not solely a power limitation — a methodological lesson for the pipeline.

The reframing is stark when the previously emphasised signals are set beside the one that was actually validated:

7.Limitations

  • Still a small, class-imbalanced, consultant-filtered cohort (33 rejects). δ ≤ ~0.20 effects remain undetectable; the Tier-B leads need more rejects to resolve.
  • Univariate screen. Does not adjust for major, academic profile, or feature overlap; answers “does this feature separate the groups,” not “does it add independent predictive value.”
  • Exposure confounding is unresolved for the small-δ features (see §5C); a length-normalized sensitivity analysis is the recommended next step before promoting any Tier-B feature.
  • Recovery dependence + a spreadsheet data-quality issue (the Vibhu Krishnan contradictory label) materially affected the prior result; the underlying outcome spreadsheet warrants a consistency pass.
  • Descriptive, not causal or representative of the Purdue applicant population.

Interpretation guardrail

All results are associational within a consultant-filtered, class-imbalanced cohort. They describe how admitted and rejected applicants in this dataset differ. They do not establish causation, and they do not show that Purdue rewards public contribution in general.

8.Conclusions & Recommendation

On the recovered, deduplicated cohort, public-contribution language is a genuine, multiplicity-robust separator of admitted vs rejected Purdue applicants (δ ≈ 0.40, medium) — the project’s first confirmed semantic finding. A coherent civic-contribution / activity-engagement cluster (leadership, service, builder, activity-hours) is suggestive but unproven and partly confounded with text length.

Next steps, in priority order

  1. Length-normalize the semantic counts (per-100-words or residualize on activities_word_count) and re-test the Tier-B cluster — the single cheapest way to tell content from exposure.
  2. Keep recovering rejects (11 rejected outcomes still lack PDFs); the Tier-B small effects sit right at the power frontier.
  3. Audit the outcome spreadsheet for further contradictory / duplicate labels (the Vibhu Krishnan case implies others may exist).
  4. Treat the logistic v2-model coefficients as superseded by this validated screen; if re-fit, use ≤4–5 predictors / penalized regression.
